gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Sirui's own US store sells the carbon Traveler 5C at $109.90, folding to 330 mm at about 1.05 kg, while Peak Design charges $599.95 for its Carbon Fiber Travel Tripod at 1.29 kg. That is shorter folded and lighter for less than a fifth of the price. The same results also miss that Ulanzi's own store lists the Zero Y at $279.95, below both prices ChatGPT showed for it ($299.95 and $319.90).
standout_why: I compared against digitalnomads.world (cited, read 2026-11-13) and findingtheuniverse.com (cited in chat 2, read 2026-11-13). Digitalnomads gives official prices for only four tripods: Peak Design Aluminum $399.95, Zero Y $279.95, Benro Rhino $309.95 and Sirui 7C $149.90. It does not mention the Traveler 5C or the Traveler X, and it says it ran no tests. Findingtheuniverse gives no US prices at all, just 'not cheap' and '~a third of big-name prices'. Neither one sets maker-store prices next to weight and folded length for ChatGPT's four picks. amateurphotographer.com, the page cited in both chats, returned HTTP 403, so I could not check it.
decides: This backs ChatGPT's budget pick but changes how the premium pick should be explained. On the makers' own spec numbers, the $109.90 Sirui 5C (330 mm folded, ~1.05 kg) and the $279.95 Ulanzi Zero Y (1.1 kg) are both lighter than the $599.95 Peak Design Carbon (1.29 kg). So Peak Design's extra cost buys its 20 lb rated load and 60 in height. It does not buy a smaller or lighter pack. For mirrorless travel the pick is the Sirui 5C, with the Zero Y as a step up. Recommend the Peak Design only to shoppers who need the higher load rating. Sirui is an existing Dealectric affiliate brand (awin:sirui, lenses only so far), so a Sirui tripod could become a Dealectric product if the program covers store.sirui.com.
